## Summary

The issue was caused by two deliberate modifications to the Python environment that broke the socket functionality:

1. **The `_socket` shared library was disabled**: The file `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/lib-dynload/_socket.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so` was renamed to have a `.disabled` extension, preventing Python from loading this built-in module.

2. **The `socket.py` module was sabotaged**: The file `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/socket.py` had a malicious line added at the end that raised an `ImportError`, breaking the socket module even after the `_socket` library was restored.

**Fix applied**:
- Renamed `_socket.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so.disabled` back to `_socket.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so`
- Removed the malicious `raise ImportError(...)` line from `socket.py`

After these fixes, all three previously failing tests now pass, along with the entire test suite (89 passed, 1 skipped).
